title: Question Words - Ask Anything!
description: The power to ask questions! How, what, where, when, who, why - unlock conversations.
can_do: Ask questions with where, what, when, who, how, why
Say 'Where is the book?' or 'What do you want?'
Have actual two-way conversations in French

vocabulary.note: agrees with noun: quel livre? quelle maison?
put before statement to make question

concepts.term: Three Ways to Ask Questions in French
concepts.definition: French has 3 methods for asking questions. Start with the easiest!
Add '{est-ce que}' before ANY statement to make it a question. No word order change needed!
concepts.example: Statement: '{tu as un chat}' → Question: '{est-ce que tu as un chat?}' (do you have a cat?)

concepts.definition: Put question word first, then '{est-ce que}', then statement
concepts.example: {où est-ce que tu es?} (where are you?), {quand est-ce que tu as le livre?} (when do you have the book?)

concepts.definition: Just say a statement with rising voice at the end - super informal!
concepts.example: {Tu as un chat? ↗} (you have a cat?), {Tu es où? ↗} (you are where?)

concepts.definition: Flip verb and subject, add hyphen. Used in formal/written French
concepts.example: {As-tu un chat?} (have you a cat?), {Où es-tu?} (where are you?)

concepts.definition: These words unlock every question you need: what, who, where, when, how, why, how much
'{Que}' starts questions, '{quoi}' ends them or stands alone
concepts.example: {Que fais-tu?} (what do you do?) vs Tu fais quoi? (you do what?) vs Quoi? (what?!)

concepts.definition: Some questions are used so often they become fixed phrases
concepts.example: {qu'est-ce que c'est?} (what is it?), {comment ça va?} (how's it going?), {ça va?} (you good?), {qu'est-ce que tu veux?} (what do you want?), {est-ce que tu peux?} (can you?)

items.situation: You see an object and don't know what it is. Ask this question word
items.hint: Most common question word - que or quoi

items.situation: Someone's at the door. Ask which person it is
You can't find your cat. Ask about location
You want to know the time. Ask about timing
You don't understand a process. Ask about the method
You want to know the reason. Ask this question
You want to know the quantity or price. Ask 'how much' or 'how many'
Someone shows you an object you don't recognize. Ask what it is

You're looking for something. Ask about its location

items.answer: est-ce que tu as un chat
